newsitem.title: USA: Steve Jobs to remain at Pixar.
newsitem.headline: Steve Jobs to remain at Pixar.

text.p: Steve Jobs, the visionary co-founder of Apple Computer Inc., has decided not to take command of the company again, news reports said Thursday.

The possibility that Jobs might return as chairman of the Cupertino, Calif.-based computer maker sent the company's stock soaring on Wall Street this week as investors were betting he could provide a spark to the troubled computer maker.

However, hopes of Jobs' return were dashed Thursday when the San Francisco Chronicle published an electronic mail message from Jobs to his workers at his new company, Pixar Animation Studios, saying he had no intention of taking the top post at Apple.

Thursday's reports came 24 hours after several news organisations, including the Chronicle, reported Jobs was about to become Apple's chairman. The reports sent the company's stock up 5 percent Wednesday. Apple rose another 12.5 cents on Thursday to close at $17.50 on Nasdaq.
"I love my job at Pixar. ... Don't pay any attention to the crazy rumours," Jobs said in the message. "That's all they are. I have no plans to leave Pixar."
Jobs could not be reached immediately for comment.
Spokeswomen at Apple and Pixar declined to comment.

Earlier this month, Apple's board forced out Gilbert Amelio, the previous chairman and chief executive, because of the company's plunging sales. Speculation immediately arose that Jobs, whom Amelio had hired as a part-time adviser in December, would become the company's new chief.
To be sure, Jobs has had extraordinary power as an adviser, playing a major part in setting Apple's strategy in trimming its product lines and hiring executives, analysts have said.

But Jobs is committed to Pixar, a thriving animation studio that has just landed a lucrative contract with the Walt Disney Co. DISN, said Keith Benjamin, analyst at investment bank Robertson Stephens & Co. in San Francisco.

"Steve has been specific in conversation with me that he spends the majority of his time at Apple helping with the search (for a new chairman and CEO), but the future of Pixar is his responsibility," Benjamin said.
"Pixar is the coolest place to work on the planet," Benjamin said. "Steve would be crazy to give that up."
